cases.name: write-edit-delete-recreate-writes-one-entry-per-commit
cases.notes: README §5.4 step 5, §5.6 step 1: a document's life in the feed — its first observation is a `created` entry carrying the head minted and the file hash; an edit a `changed` entry under the new head; a gone path a `deleted` entry with no head and no hash (the feed row's reason is `observed deletion`); bytes observed again at the tombstoned path revive the row — a `created` entry again (§5.6 "Re-creation"), under the revival's head. One feed row per commit, `seq` dense from 1, `batch_id` the row's own commit (every batch here has one committing member), `plan_id` NULL on the observe path; the recorder's `commits` row shares each id, epoch and seq (H4).

cases.name: batch-id-is-the-first-committing-member
cases.notes: README §5.4 step 5 (D4): `batch_id` is the commit id of the FIRST member of the batch that committed — an echo commits nothing and names no batch. Batch 1 (two members) → both rows carry c_0. Batch 2: a.md is an echo (no commit), b.md's edit commits first (c_2, its own batch id), the gone path's tombstone and d.md's creation follow under c_2; a gone member with no live doc commits nothing. The status row the sync layer writes is spec/sync's; this suite projects the feed.

cases.name: retention-floors-prune-old-rows-beyond-the-entry-floor
cases.notes: README §7.4: a row is prunable when it is older than `feed.retain_days` AND more than `feed.retain_entries` rows of its epoch are newer than it — both floors, by `ts` against gc's clock. With `retain_days: 0` and `retain_entries: 2` five commits leave three rows after gc (seq 3–5: the row with exactly two newer rows is not "more than"), `feed_pruned: 2`, their entries gone with them; `oldest` moves to 3 while `commits` keeps every row (the log is history). Set through the repository's settings layer (spec/sync §3; the `exec` step is the fixture's device for a settings write). The entries invariant F1 holds because every retained document's head is in a retained entry.

sql: UPDATE repos SET settings = '{"feed": {"retain_days": 0, "retain_entries": 2}}' WHERE slug = 'fixture'

cases.name: retention-days-floor-keeps-young-rows
cases.notes: README §7.4: the day floor alone keeps a row — with `retain_entries: 0` every row but the newest is beyond the entry floor, yet a gc one day after the commits prunes nothing (`retain_days` is the default 10), and a gc eleven days after prunes every row but the newest (`feed_pruned: 2`). Both floors must be passed; the cap (`max_entries`) is not involved.

sql: UPDATE repos SET settings = '{"feed": {"retain_entries": 0}}' WHERE slug = 'fixture'

cases.name: cap-prunes-at-write-time-regardless-of-the-floors
cases.notes: README §7.4: `feed.max_entries` is enforced inside the transaction that appends a feed row, oldest first, regardless of the floors — a feed never exceeds `max_entries + 1` rows. With `max_entries: 1` (and `retain_entries: 1`, the policy's lower bound) four commits leave two rows (seq 3, 4) without any gc; the gc afterwards finds nothing more to prune under the default `retain_days`. The pruned rows' commits stay in the recorder's log.

sql: UPDATE repos SET settings = '{"feed": {"retain_entries": 1, "max_entries": 1}}' WHERE slug = 'fixture'

cases.name: prune-never-takes-the-newest-row
cases.notes: README §7.4: pruning never deletes the row with the greatest `seq` — at `retain_entries: 0` and `retain_days: 0` a gc leaves exactly the head row (`feed_pruned` = rows − 1), so `oldest == head` and a consumer at `cursor = head − 1` is still served (every entry after it is present); `changes_since` from 0 on such a feed shows the gap through `oldest` (spec/surface §3).

sql: UPDATE repos SET settings = '{"feed": {"retain_days": 0, "retain_entries": 0}}' WHERE slug = 'fixture'

cases.name: remint-epoch-starts-the-feed-over
cases.notes: §7.5 (17.0): the epoch re-mint of a restore / rebuild-from-files — two commits under ep_0 (seq 1, 2), then `remint_epoch` mints ep_1 and deletes every feed row and entry of the repository; the next commit is seq 1 of ep_1, and the recorder's `commits` keep their old epoch (c_0, c_1 under ep_0; H4 compares the retained feed only). The projection's `feed`/`feed_entries` are the current epoch's; the `ep` claims are omitted like `rp`.
